title: Can PDRN be pushed through the skin with a weak current? A computer model of PDRN iontophoresis (follow-up to the topical PDRN entry)
headline: A September 2026 modelling paper says PDRN's large size limits how far it passes the skin barrier, and models a weak-current device to help; it is a simulation with one measured input and no human outcome.
evidenceTier: Computational model plus a diffusion-cell measurement; abstract read; free full text not opened
fit: Context for a delivery question that the earlier PDRN entry left open. Nothing to try; no device or product was tested.
displaces: Fits nowhere: no product or device was tested in people.
estimateNote: Prices marked EST are my guesses, not looked up.
summaryPoints: Abstract (read): authors state PDRN's large molecular size limits noninvasive delivery; they build a three-layer skin model (stratum corneum, epidermis, dermis) using the Nernst-Planck equation, with a diffusion coefficient from diffusion-cell experiments and the electric charge estimated from earlier double-stranded-DNA reports.

The model compares passive diffusion with iontophoresis (cathode) across current, concentration and time, and reports a depth-dependent shift in the dominant transport mechanism; it reports agreement metrics with experimental permeation data (RMSD, MAPE, R2) without numbers in the abstract.
One author lists Trans Bio Lab Co. Ltd. as an affiliation. No human outcomes, no skin-tone data, no product.
Why it matters: last run's topical PDRN entry flagged that delivery into living human dermis was not shown; this paper agrees that delivery is the limiting question and does not answer it.
fitLine: Delivery science, not an outcome study.
